claims.text: NVIDIA, Microsoft and Meta published "Open Weights and American AI Leadership" on July 24, 2026; the list grew from 25 to 50 signatories in a day, adding OpenAI, Google and AMD.
Anthropic and Amazon are the only notable holdouts as of July 26.

The letter's own text draws a specific line: distillation is 'a widely used technique for model improvement, evaluation, and validation,' and concerns should be addressed through 'targeted legal and commercial frameworks rather than sweeping restrictions.'

Michael Kratsios wrote: 'We have information that Moonshot AI distilled Anthropic's Fable for the development of its K3 model,' calling it 'large-scale, covert industrial distillation aimed at stealing proprietary U.S. technology and undermining American research.'

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent tells Fox Business the administration is 'finding watermarks of our U.S. large language models on many of the Chinese models' and warns sanctions and Entity List designations are 'on the table'.

In November 2025, NVIDIA and Microsoft jointly committed to invest up to $10 billion and up to $5 billion respectively in Anthropic, tied to Anthropic purchasing $30 billion of Azure compute and up to 1 gigawatt of NVIDIA Grace Blackwell/Vera Rubin capacity.
The round reportedly pushed Anthropic's valuation to roughly $350 billion, about double its prior mark.
Google's separate ~14% Anthropic stake is contractually capped at 15% with no voting rights.

NVIDIA publicly attacked Anthropic's Diffusion Rule position, arguing American firms 'should focus on innovation... rather than tell tall tales that... electronics are somehow smuggled in baby bumps'.
DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis first posted general backing for 'a strong and secure open ecosystem,' citing Gemma's growth, without Google appearing on the official signatory list.
Google's own 2024 comment to NTIA said 'the benefits of many open models still significantly outweigh the risks'.
Braden Hancock of the Laude Institute told TechCrunch: 'You can't distill that much data, train a model, and release it in two weeks.'
In February 2026 Anthropic accused DeepSeek, Moonshot and MiniMax of building roughly 16 million interactions through about 24,000 fake accounts to distill Claude.
David Sacks: 'The leading closed labs, already a duopoly in terms of AI model revenue, want the government to eliminate their open source competition.'
A RAND review found only 1 of 37 open model families it assessed met all four proposed criteria for proportional safety evaluation.
NVIDIA was Hugging Face's single largest open-model contributor in 2025, with roughly 650 open models and 250 datasets, in the words of NVIDIA's own Bryan Catanzaro.
Alibaba's Qwen alone reportedly accounts for roughly 942 million Hugging Face downloads against a combined ~56 million for all US open entrants.
Chinese models at 46.4% of OpenRouter token volume against 35.7% for US models as of July 20.
Booz Allen analysis found Qwen3-Coder +130%, MiniMax M2.5 +20%, DeepSeek V4-Pro +5% more vulnerable code under a US-government persona.
NVDA and MSFT daily close prices, July 22-24 2026 (line-chart: 212.06/208.76/206.84 and 390.34/381.58/381.70).
GOOGL's steep 7.4% single-day drop happened on July 23, driven by Alphabet raising its 2026 capex guidance to $195-205 billion.
Roughly three-quarters of Anthropic's revenue is API-token based.
